# Personal Finance App — Chapter 11 (capstone, part 1 of 2)

## Context

Existing zero-based-budgeting tools and spreadsheet templates don't fit how the user wants to manage money. Zero-based tools force every dollar into a category but hide the simple "income − expenses = leftover" number and don't make it easy to redirect leftover funds between categories. Spreadsheet templates are transaction-heavy with weak category-level and high-level analysis. She wants **awareness budgeting**: always see where money is going, decide where leftovers should go, and proactively realign spending to priorities — not a reactive, alert-only tool.

This build doubles as the running capstone project for chapters 11 and 12 of her book ("AI First Java Programming"), built via AI-paired development in this repo. `chapter11-code-tests/` is currently empty. Sibling chapters (`chapter8-code-tests/music-playlist`, `chapter9-code-tests/farmers-market-app`) establish the house style: one Maven module per chapter, Java 17, JUnit 5.10.2 as the only dependency, a flat `com.example.<pkg>` package, plain Java classes (no config-file indirection), and a README with a one-line "Quick start."

Chapter 11 scope (confirmed with user) is intentionally an MVP slice of the full capstone:
1. Record and display transactions
2. Group transactions by category and compare against targets
3. Flag over-budget categories and surface warnings
4. Savings goals + allocate what's left over
5. A full month summary view
6. Track spread expenses (annual subscriptions) and long-term contract dates/payments

Chapter 12 (not built now, but design must not block it) will add: moving leftover between categories, multi-month trend/history analysis, and priority/lifestyle alignment insights.

Confirmed decisions:
- **Desktop GUI**, not console — open to any library but wants nice UX without piling on dependencies.
- **No database** — simple file-based persistence for a first version.
- **Calendar month** budget cycle.

## Approach

**GUI: JavaFX, hand-built scenes (no FXML).** JavaFX ships `PieChart`/`BarChart` for free, which directly serves the "high-level analysis" goal without a third-party charting library (the Swing alternative would need JFreeChart to match that). The local JDK (Zulu 25) doesn't bundle JavaFX, so it arrives via Maven either way — `org.openjfx:javafx-controls` + the `javafx-maven-plugin` (so `README.md`'s quick start stays `mvn javafx:run`, avoiding module-path hand-holding). Skip `javafx-fxml`/FXML entirely — one more file type and syntax per screen isn't worth it against the existing "plain Java, one class one responsibility" house style; screens are built directly in Java (`VBox`, `TableView`, etc.).

**Persistence: hand-rolled pipe-delimited text files, no library.** One file per entity, stored under `~/.personal-finance-app/data/` (not inside the project folder, since this is meant for real personal use across sessions and the project dir could get rebuilt). Pipe (`|`) delimiter avoids collisions with commas in descriptions without needing quoting/escaping logic. Each file starts with a `#` header-comment line documenting its columns. Load: skip and log malformed lines rather than failing the whole file. Save: write to a temp file and atomically rename over the original, so a crash mid-write can't corrupt data. Write-through on every mutating action (no explicit Save button).

**Money as `BigDecimal`, never `double`** — this app's entire premise is trustworthy totals (leftover, over-budget flags); floating-point drift would undermine that immediately.

**Design for Chapter 12 up front (cheap now, expensive later):** thread a `YearMonth` parameter through every service method (`BudgetService`, `MonthSummaryService`, `RecurringObligationService`) instead of having them silently assume "current month." Chapter 11's UI just always passes `YearMonth.now()`. This means Chapter 12's multi-month history view only needs a month-picker + loop over existing calls — no service rework. Similarly, leftover-allocation for savings goals is recorded in its own log (`GoalContribution`), not mixed into the transaction ledger — Chapter 12's cross-category reallocation follows the same "separate adjustment log" pattern.

### Package/class list — `com.example.finance`

**Model**
- `TransactionType` — enum `INCOME`, `EXPENSE`
- `RecurringFrequency` — enum `MONTHLY`, `QUARTERLY`, `ANNUAL` (knows months-per-cycle)
- `Category` — name, monthlyTarget (`BigDecimal`), `TransactionType`
- `Transaction` — id, `LocalDate` date, `TransactionType`, categoryName, `BigDecimal` amount, description
- `SavingsGoal` — name, targetAmount, currentAmount (derived, updated via contributions), optional targetDate
- `GoalContribution` — date, goalName, amount — the leftover-allocation log
- `RecurringObligation` — name, categoryName, amount, `RecurringFrequency`, nextDueDate

**Persistence** (identical shape per entity: load/save/add; hand-rolled pipe-delimited I/O)
- `DataPaths` — single source of truth for `~/.personal-finance-app/data/` and per-entity filenames
- `CategoryRepository`, `TransactionRepository`, `SavingsGoalRepository`, `GoalContributionRepository`, `RecurringObligationRepository`

**Service/logic layer** (unit-testable, no JavaFX dependency; each takes a `YearMonth`)
- `BudgetService` — per-category totals, leftover = income − expenses, over-budget flags
- `RecurringObligationService` — monthly-equivalent per obligation/category, upcoming-payments (configurable lookahead window)
- `SavingsGoalService` — goal progress, "allocate leftover to goal" action (records a `GoalContribution`, validates against available leftover)
- `MonthSummaryService` — thin facade assembling the above for the dashboard

**JavaFX UI** (one `*View` per screen, constructed from services only — never touches repositories or does arithmetic itself)
- `MainApp` — `Application` entry point; builds repositories/services once, hosts a `TabPane` of the views below
- `TransactionEntryView` — entry form + table of the month's transactions (scope item 1)
- `CategorySummaryView` — category vs. target vs. actual table, over-budget rows highlighted, warning banner (scope items 2–3)
- `SavingsGoalsView` — goals with progress, leftover readout, "allocate to goal" action (scope item 4)
- `MonthSummaryView` — leftover figure + `PieChart` (spend by category) + `BarChart` (target vs. actual), over-budget/upcoming callouts (scope item 5)
- `RecurringObligationsView` — obligations table + upcoming-payments list (scope item 6)

### File layout

```
chapter11-code-tests/
  personal-finance-app/
    pom.xml
    README.md
    src/main/java/com/example/finance/
      TransactionType.java  RecurringFrequency.java
      Category.java  Transaction.java  SavingsGoal.java
      GoalContribution.java  RecurringObligation.java
      DataPaths.java
      CategoryRepository.java  TransactionRepository.java
      SavingsGoalRepository.java  GoalContributionRepository.java
      RecurringObligationRepository.java
      BudgetService.java  RecurringObligationService.java
      SavingsGoalService.java  MonthSummaryService.java
      MainApp.java
      TransactionEntryView.java  CategorySummaryView.java
      SavingsGoalsView.java  MonthSummaryView.java
      RecurringObligationsView.java
    src/test/java/com/example/finance/
      TransactionRepositoryTest.java
      BudgetServiceTest.java  RecurringObligationServiceTest.java
      SavingsGoalServiceTest.java  MonthSummaryServiceTest.java
```

Divergences from the sibling-chapter template: `pom.xml` adds the JavaFX deps + `javafx-maven-plugin` (mainClass `com.example.finance.MainApp`); README's quick start becomes `mvn javafx:run` (plain `java -cp` won't work against JavaFX without module-path flags) and should note that data lives in `~/.personal-finance-app/data/`, outside the project folder. No `src/main/resources/` for now (no FXML/CSS).

### Build order

1. **Skeleton, no UI** — `pom.xml`, all model classes, `DataPaths`, all five repositories. Verify with a round-trip test/throwaway main: add → save → reload → print.
2. **`BudgetService` + `TransactionEntryView` + `CategorySummaryView`** — first real GUI milestone: enter transactions, see category totals and an over-budget row light up.
3. **`MonthSummaryService` + `MonthSummaryView`** — leftover figure + the two charts rendering from real data; the "awareness budgeting" payoff moment, worth its own milestone.
4. **`SavingsGoalService` + `SavingsGoalsView`** — create a goal, allocate leftover, watch progress update and leftover shrink.
5. **`RecurringObligationService` + `RecurringObligationsView`** — add an annual subscription, see its monthly-equivalent feed into the right category's actual-vs-target (loops back to milestone 2) and appear in upcoming payments.
6. **`MainApp` wiring** — assemble all views into tabs, final error-handling/README pass.

### Tests

In scope: `TransactionRepositoryTest` (save/load round-trip + malformed-line-is-skipped, representative of all repos), `BudgetServiceTest` (totals, leftover, over-budget boundary at exactly target), `RecurringObligationServiceTest` (monthly-equivalent per frequency, upcoming-payments window boundary), `SavingsGoalServiceTest` (allocation reduces leftover/increases progress; over-allocation handling), `MonthSummaryServiceTest` (facade wiring). Out of scope: `MainApp` and all `*View` classes — matches sibling chapters (none test their `*App` entry points) and avoids introducing a JavaFX test-framework dependency.

## Verification

- `mvn -q test` — all five service/repository test classes pass.
- `mvn javafx:run` — walk the golden path manually: add income + a few expense transactions across categories, confirm the category table and leftover figure update, push one category over its target and confirm the warning/highlight appears, create a savings goal and allocate leftover to it, add a recurring obligation (e.g. an annual subscription) and confirm its monthly-equivalent shows up in the right category and in the upcoming-payments list, check the month summary charts reflect all of the above.
- Confirm data survives a restart: close and re-run `mvn javafx:run`, verify previously entered transactions/goals/obligations reload from `~/.personal-finance-app/data/`.

## Context

Existing zero-based-budgeting tools and spreadsheet templates don't fit how the user wants to manage money. Zero-based tools force every dollar into a category but hide the simple "income − expenses = leftover" number and don't make it easy to redirect leftover funds between categories. Spreadsheet templates are transaction-heavy with weak category-level and high-level analysis. She wants **awareness budgeting**: always see where money is going, decide where leftovers should go, and proactively realign spending to priorities — not a reactive, alert-only tool.

This build doubles as the running capstone project for chapters 11 and 12 of her book ("AI First Java Programming"), built via AI-paired development in this repo. `chapter11-code-tests/` is currently empty. Sibling chapters (`chapter8-code-tests/music-playlist`, `chapter9-code-tests/farmers-market-app`) establish the house style: one Maven module per chapter, Java 17, JUnit 5.10.2 as the only dependency, a flat `com.example.<pkg>` package, plain Java classes (no config-file indirection), and a README with a one-line "Quick start."

Chapter 11 scope (confirmed with user) is intentionally an MVP slice of the full capstone:
1. Record and display transactions
2. Group transactions by category and compare against targets
3. Flag over-budget categories and surface warnings
4. Savings goals + allocate what's left over
5. A full month summary view
6. Track spread expenses (annual subscriptions) and long-term contract dates/payments

Chapter 12 (not built now, but design must not block it) will add: moving leftover between categories, multi-month trend/history analysis, and priority/lifestyle alignment insights.

Confirmed decisions:
- **Desktop GUI**, not console — open to any library but wants nice UX without piling on dependencies.
- **No database** — simple file-based persistence for a first version.
- **Calendar month** budget cycle.

## Approach

**GUI: JavaFX, hand-built scenes (no FXML).** JavaFX ships `PieChart`/`BarChart` for free, which directly serves the "high-level analysis" goal without a third-party charting library (the Swing alternative would need JFreeChart to match that). The local JDK (Zulu 25) doesn't bundle JavaFX, so it arrives via Maven either way — `org.openjfx:javafx-controls` + the `javafx-maven-plugin` (so `README.md`'s quick start stays `mvn javafx:run`, avoiding module-path hand-holding). Skip `javafx-fxml`/FXML entirely — one more file type and syntax per screen isn't worth it against the existing "plain Java, one class one responsibility" house style; screens are built directly in Java (`VBox`, `TableView`, etc.).

**Persistence: hand-rolled pipe-delimited text files, no library.** One file per entity, stored under `~/.personal-finance-app/data/` (not inside the project folder, since this is meant for real personal use across sessions and the project dir could get rebuilt). Pipe (`|`) delimiter avoids collisions with commas in descriptions without needing quoting/escaping logic. Each file starts with a `#` header-comment line documenting its columns. Load: skip and log malformed lines rather than failing the whole file. Save: write to a temp file and atomically rename over the original, so a crash mid-write can't corrupt data. Write-through on every mutating action (no explicit Save button).

**Money as `BigDecimal`, never `double`** — this app's entire premise is trustworthy totals (leftover, over-budget flags); floating-point drift would undermine that immediately.

**Design for Chapter 12 up front (cheap now, expensive later):** thread a `YearMonth` parameter through every service method (`BudgetService`, `MonthSummaryService`, `RecurringObligationService`) instead of having them silently assume "current month." Chapter 11's UI just always passes `YearMonth.now()`. This means Chapter 12's multi-month history view only needs a month-picker + loop over existing calls — no service rework. **`Category` stays flat — no `List<Transaction>`.** `Transaction` already links to its category by name (a plain string, not an object reference) specifically so reloading from separate files never requires re-wiring a stale object graph. Caching a transaction list on `Category` would create a second source of truth that can drift (add/delete a transaction and forget to update the cached list; reload the two files in a different order and the list is stale) and it's ambiguous in scope anyway (all-time vs. current-month). `BudgetService` already filters transactions by `categoryName` + `YearMonth` on demand — that's where this association belongs.

- `Transaction` — id, `LocalDate` date, `TransactionType`, categoryName, `BigDecimal` amount, description
- `SavingsGoal` — name, targetAmount, currentAmount (derived, updated via contributions), optional targetDate
- `GoalContribution` — date, goalName, amount — the leftover-allocation log
